title: VPC sidecar 'usage shuttle' for intermittent air-gapped exports and quota-resilient replay
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Customers running Private/VPC deployments in restricted or intermittently connected networks need a robust, auditable way to export usage and quota change data to Redwood without continuous connectivity. Existing offline collectors produce large monolithic bundles that are hard to resume after partial failures and cause duplicate accounting when retries overlap. Goal: Ship a lightweight sidecar daemon (usage-shuttle) that maintains an append-only local ledger, emits compact signed delta manifests for outward transfer, and supports deterministic replay with deduplication and ledger checkpointing.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar runs in customer VPC (sidecar container) and writes append-only entries for each outgoing usage event and quota decision
Exports are produced as compact delta manifests (not full bundles) with monotonic sequence ranges and Ed25519 signatures
Server-side reconciliation can idempotently apply delta manifests and reject duplicate or out-of-order windows
CLI/agent supports resume-after-failure: partial manifests are reconciled and the sidecar can retransmit missing ranges without double-counting
Reconciliation runbook documented in Confluence and tested in an air-gap test harness (see links)
tasks: Design append-only local ledger format and minimal metadata header
Implement sidecar writer and rotating WAL with compaction thresholds
Implement atomic manifest emitter with signed sequence window and manifest index
Add local rate-limiter fallback that enforces soft quotas when control-plane unreachable
Server reconciliation: add idempotent applier and sequence-window validation logic
End-to-end test harness: emulate intermittent connectivity and partial manifest delivery
Docs: onboarding, security model, key rotation, and runbook for manual replay
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC sketched — ledger + delta-manifest approach chosen to avoid monolithic bundle replays. Trade-off: slightly larger metadata vs robust resumability. (Aisha)
2026-03-11: Prototype WAL writer implemented — local schema 'usgWAL v1' with monotonic counter and event checksums. WAL rotation triggered at 10MB. (Liam)
2026-03-12: Spike for signature scheme completed: Ed25519 chosen for small key size and community support. Added header fields: sidecar_id, seq_start, seq_end, prev_manifest_hash. (Liam)

2026-03-13: Server applier patch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/412 — implements seq-window validation and idempotent apply. Need security review for signature verification and key management flow. (Aisha)

2026-03-13: Discovered potential race where two sidecar replicas could emit overlapping seq windows after split-brain; plan to add a leader lease for sidecar instances per node via local lockfile. (Liam)
comments: PM feedback (2026-03-11): Ensure per-customer replay visibility in Console; we need a timeline UI for 'offline ingestion gaps' — link to mock: https://drive.redwood.com/pm/offline-ingest-mock
Security note (2026-03-12): Key rotation story must support both customer-managed KMS keys and Redwood-managed ephemeral signing keys; add to scope. (Olivia Chen, Security)
Design review (2026-03-13): DES-197 to follow up on minimal manifest payload structure and UX for operators to trigger replays. (Santiago, Design)
Engineering review (2026-03-13): Consider adding a compact bloom filter per manifest to speed duplicate detection on server side for large-scale customers. (Review comment on PR 412)

Customer observed: 'sometimes our on-prem gateway restarts and we lose half a bundle' — this ticket should prioritize resume correctness and small manifest sizes to reduce re-send cost. (reported by CS lead)
implementation_notes: Ledger entry atomicity: use write-ahead file + fsync per manifest commit to minimize window of partial writes
Manifest rotation: prefer delta windows of 1k-10k events depending on event size; allow operator override via env var SIDE_CAR_MAX_EVENTS
Dedup key: (customer_id, sidecar_id, seq_start, seq_end) and manifest hash; server keeps sliding watermark per sidecar_id
Backpressure: when control-plane unreachable, sidecar should switch from real-time upload to local retention and apply local soft quotas to avoid customer overruns
Observability: emit metrics - wal_bytes, manifests_emitted, manifests_failed, replay_attempts, last_seq_applied
CLI: redwoodctl usage-shuttle push/replay/status to support manual operations in high-touch onboarding
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate application of events on partial replays => Mitigation: server rejects overlapping seq windows and keeps per-sidecar monotonic watermarks
Risk: Sidecar key compromise => Mitigation: integrate customer KMS or HSM-backed signing; add revocation manifest and server-side acceptance window
Risk: Large backlog on long air-gaps => Mitigation: allow sidecar to emit compressed manifests and server to accept chunked application with integrity checks
Risk: Split-brain with multiple sidecars => Mitigation: leader lease + local lockfile; fall back to server-resolved highest-seq applier with out-of-band operator confirmation
